fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. They broke up the sacred pillars, chopped down the Asherah poles, and tore down the high places and altars. The text says they kept at it "…until they had utterly destroyed them all." They took the job seriously, and that's a whole lot of demolition.

It's the other direction, friend. These Israelites had been in attendance for the celebration in Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 30:13), and in the cities of Judah they tore down altars. They tore down the high places too. Nobody picked up a hammer to build anything new in this verse.

That's the one, baker. The text says the king contributed from his own possessions for the regular morning and evening burnt offerings, and for the Sabbaths, New Moons and appointed feasts. That came from Hezekiah's own possessions, not from somebody else's. It was all done as written in the Law of the LORD.
Close, but the verse names someone else. It says the king contributed from his own possessions for these offerings. The priests are the ones serving. Hezekiah is the one who contributed.

Right, baker. Hezekiah commanded the people in Jerusalem to make a contribution so the priests and Levites "…could devote themselves to the Law of the LORD." The gift is there so they can give themselves to that work. I like that. It's like a friend covering your shift so you can finally get to the thing you've been trying to focus on.

Nothing sneaky is in this verse, baker. The text says the Israelites "generously provided" the firstfruits of the grain, new wine, oil and honey. It never says anyone gave in secret. What it does say is that they brought in an abundance, a tithe of everything.

Seventh month, baker. The text says they began building up the heaps in the third month and finished in the seventh. That's a long stretch of bringing and stacking. I've waited a good while for a pan of cookies to cool when I wasn't paying attention.
The verse doesn't show any counting, friend. It says that when Hezekiah and his officials came and viewed the heaps, they blessed the LORD and His people Israel. Blessing is what the text gives us.

That's not what Azariah says, baker. Azariah, the chief priest of the household of Zadok, says they've had enough to eat since the people began to bring their contributions into the house of the LORD. His reason is "…the LORD has blessed His people…" Keeping back portions never comes up in what he says.
